title: Surgical Rollouts - UX canvas & playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact UX canvas and playbook for a "surgical" rollouts experience in the Console. The idea: give platform and product teams fine-grained, low-friction controls to route tiny slices of traffic to model variants, do multi-dimensional A/B experiments, and specify automatic fallback/rollback policies that are auditable and predictable. This doc focuses on wireframe-level UI flows, microcopy, and a prioritized grooming backlog for implementation iterations.

Design goals (high level):
- Make targeted rollouts dead-simple: by customer, route, auth-token, or custom attribute.
- Expose a small set of safe defaults for non-experts while allowing power users to specify complex conditions.
- Surface live health signals and deterministic rollback triggers in the same panel where you author the rollout.
- Keep audits and change history visible and exportable.

Core concepts (user-facing vocabulary):
- Release unit: what you are rolling out (model + version + config bundle).
- Target slice: the traffic subset (percentage, API key, route, tag-based cohort).
- Warmup window: optional period where we send probe/synthetic requests and ramp KV cache.
- Fallback policy: prioritized list of fallback variants and how to trigger them.
- Safety thresholds: explicit latency/error/quality budgets to auto-rollback or auto-route to fallback.

Wireframe overview (three-pane modal + inline route card):
1) Trigger modal (Create rollout) - modal width 1100px, two-column grid
   Left column (authoring):
   - Title input (single line) + optional description (small).
   - Release unit selector: dropdown with search and quick-preview metrics (tokens/sec, avg latency, quantization tag).
   - Targeting block: radio buttons for % rollout | API keys | customer attributes | route pattern. When % is selected, show a slider with numeric input.
   - Advanced button -> expands YAML-like condition builder (for power users).
   - Warmup toggle: when enabled, show duration and probe cadence (e.g., 30s probes, 10 requests/probe).

   Right column (safety & observability):
   - Live health toggles: latency threshold (ms), 5xx rate (%), quality regression (eval-set drift %). Each has an input + tooltip explaining impact.
   - Fallback policy editor: choose fallback targets in priority order. Each fallback row has a selector + preconditions (e.g., only route if latency > X AND 5xx > Y).
   - Rollout schedule: immediate or cron-style (date/time + timezone).
   - Preview panel: shows estimated impact (tokens routed, customer count) and quick list of linked dashboards.

2) Line-item route card (in Routes list) - condensed inline control
   - Compact on/off toggle, % slider (small), last change timestamp, and small health sparkline. Clicking opens the full modal.
   - Microcopy: "Use 'surgical rollout' to test a model on a controlled group (no more than 5% recommended)."

3) Live rollout details (single panel)
   - Top: timeline of rollout phases (created -> warmup -> ramp -> steady -> rollback/fallback) with color-coded states. Each node is clickable to expand audit info.
   - Middle: live metrics row (latency p50/p95, 5xx rate, tokens/min, eval quality delta) with small colored badges that match safety thresholds.
   - Bottom: decision log (human + automated actions) showing triggers that caused changes, with links to the exact config snapshot.

Interactions and edge cases:
- Simulated preview: before saving, users can run a "Dry run" that runs the rollout config against historical traffic for a short window to estimate cache-warmup benefit and risk. This calls an offline simulator service (backend ticket: JIRA-RND-1229).
- Overlapping rollouts: when two rollouts target the same route, show a conflict resolver that displays precedence (by explicit priority, creation time, or manual tie-break). Warn if combined percent > 100%.
- Emergency rollback: big red anchor button that performs immediate fallback to next policy target and flags the rollout as incident-linked. Ask for one confirmation phrase (microcopy: "Confirm emergency fallback for <rollout-name>").
- Partial failures during warmup: if synthetic probe success < 80%, automatically pause the rollout and notify the author via email + slack webhook.

Microcopy and accessibility notes:
- Keep copy brief and action-oriented: e.g., "Ramp to 2% over 10m" instead of "Start the rollout and increase traffic..."
- Tooltips should include short examples (e.g., attribute selector: "customer tier == 'beta' OR email endswith '@acme.com'").
- ARIA labels for sliders and critical actions. Color should not be the only signal for safety (use icons + text).

Observability hooks (what to show in the UI):
- Real-time traces link (per token or aggregated), small sample generator to replay failing requests.
- Eval-set drift metric derived from a pinned prompt set; show the small table with examples where outputs diverged.
- Cost estimate: add a tokens-cost delta estimate for the rollout (per hour/day).

Backlog grooming (ordered):
1) M0: Create basic rollout modal + inline route card (MVP) - requires release-unit selector + % slider + basic fallback selector. (Priority: P0, est: 3 sprints)
   - Subtasks: wireframe->prototype, API contract for rollout object, UI validations, simple audit log. Linked: JIRA-RND-1231.
2) M1: Safety thresholds + automated rollback actions - integrate with metrics ingestion and implement deterministic rollback engine. (Priority: P0, est: 2 sprints)
   - Needs: SRE signoff on rollback semantics, monitoring playbook entry. Linked: CONFLUENCE-7632.
3) M2: Warmup probes and dry-run simulator - backend service + UI to configure probe cadence and show simulated outcomes. (Priority: P1, est: 2 sprints)
4) M3: A/B experiment scaffolding - richer experiment analytics and per-cohort segmentation in UI + comparison report. (Priority: P1, est: 3 sprints)
5) M4: Overlap/conflict resolver and precedence rules - UI for visualizing interacting rollouts. (Priority: P2, est: 1 sprint)
6) M5: Audit/export + compliance view - CSV export of decision log + links to signed-off approvals for private deployments. (Priority: P2, est: 1 sprint)

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What are the canonical safety signals for "quality"? (eval-set drift, user feedback, human labeling). We should finalize metric definitions with Applied ML.
- How granular should the "target slice" grammar be in the GUI vs YAML mode? Start with simple builders and add advanced YAML later.
- Incident integration: should emergency rollback automatically open an incident in PagerDuty or create a ticket in the customer's ITSM?

Telemetry and success metrics (for product):
- Time-to-first-canary: target < 5 minutes from create->active for % <= 1%.
- % rollouts using automated fallback vs manual rollback (target: 70% automated after 3 months).
- Reduction in user-reported regressions attributable to rollouts (goal: -40% YOY for teams using rollouts).

Appendix: short copy samples for UI fields:
- "Rollout name": required, e.g., 'search-v2-canary-2024-11-05'
- "Warmup (optional)": "Send synthetic probe traffic to warm KV caches and validate correctness before real users are routed."
- "Fallback policy": "When a safety threshold is breached, automatically route requests to the highest-priority compatible variant."
- Emergency button: "Emergency fallback — route all traffic to fallback A (confirm with phrase)"

Next steps for this doc:
- Review with Applied ML (Maya) for quality signal definitions (action: Maya to add sample eval-set by 2024-12-10).
- Prototype screens in Figma -> link to PR (Elliot owns). Create usability test plan with 6 engineers and 3 CS customers.

Notes to implementation team:
- Keep server-side rollout spec deterministic and fully serializable. UI should only manipulate the spec as text under the hood for auditability.
- Default suggested % for a canary should be conservative (0.5-2%). Power users can override but must check a confirmation box.

Authors and context:
- Drafted during 2024 Q4 product planning sessions; intended as a bridge between current console capabilities and a more advanced rollout orchestration suite.

End of doc.
